FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft was finalized 
by the Cordage Sectional Committee and approved by the Textiles Division Council. 


Jute is a long, soft, shiny vegetable fibre that can be spun into coarse, strong threads. Jute twines are mostly used 
in packing and stitching. Other than this, it is also used for decorative purposes. 


The second revision of this standard has been published in 1984. This revision has been made in the light of 
experience gained since its publication and to incorporate the following major changes: 


a) Requirement for identification of material has been incorporated; 

b) Atmospheric conditions for conditioning and testing are specified in this standard; 
c) The test method for measuring the lubricant in the twine has been specified; 

d) Marking clause has been modified; 

e) Amendment has been incorporated; and 

f) References to Indian standards have been updated. 


The composition of the committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is listed in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places 
retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 1912 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


TEXTILES — COUNTRY JUTE TWINE — SPECIFICATION 
( Third Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of 
country jute twines of eight varieties used for 
packing, mouth stitching of bags and other 
miscellaneous purposes. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of this standard. At the time of 
publication, the editions indicated were valid. All 
standards are subject to revision, and parties to 
agreements based on this standard are encouraged to 
investigate the possibility of applying the most 
recent editions of the standards indicated in 
Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the definitions 
given in IS 3871 shall apply. 


4 ATMOSPHERIC CONDITIONS FOR 
CONDITIONING AND TESTS 


4.1 The tests shall normally be carried out under 
prevailing atmospheric conditions. In all cases of 
dispute, however, the tests shall be carried out on 
samples that have been conditioned for 24 h in a 
standard atmosphere at (65 + 2) percent relative 
humidity and (27 + 2) °C temperature as prescribed 
in IS 6359. Where practicable the tests shall be 
carried out in the standard conditioning atmosphere, 
otherwise they shall be carried out as quickly as 
possible but not exceeding 15 min after removal of 
the test pieces from the conditioning atmosphere. 


5 MANUFACTURE 
5.1 Jute Fibre 
The jute fibre used in the manufacture of the twine 


shall be free from defects like roots and specks and 
shall be well carded. 


5.2 Yarn 


Jute yarn used for making the twines shall be well 
and evenly spun with Z twist. 


5.3 Twine 


The twines shall be made of the required number of 
yarns twisted together with S twist. It shall be well 
and evenly twisted and shall be free from defects. 


5.4 Skein 


Each skein of twine shall be continuous in its length 
and shall not contain any loose ends. 


5.5 Lubricating Material 


For the purpose of dressing the fibre, lubricating 
material not exceeding 8 percent of the mass of the 
twine in a skein may be used. The lubricant content 
in the twine shall be tested as per the method 
specified in IS 7071. However, no weighting or 
loading material shall be added. 


5.6 Moisture Regain 

A maximum of 16 percent moisture regain in the 
twines shall be permissible when tested by the 
appropriate method. 


5.7 Contract Moisture Regain 


The contract moisture regain of the jute twine shall 
be 16 percent. 


6 REQUIREMENTS 


6.1 The twine shall conform to the requirements 
specified in Table 1. 


6.2 Fibre Identification 
The material of twine that is jute fibre shall be 


identified by the confirmatory test as specified in 
IS 667. 


IS 1912 : 2023

7 SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR 7.2 The conformity of a lot to the requirements of 
CONFORMITY this standard shall be determined on the basis of tests 
carried out on the samples selected from the lot. 
7.1 Lot 
7.3 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer 
The number of bales of jute twine of the same and the seller, the number of bales to be selected at 
construction delivered to one buyer against one random from a lot shall be in accordance with 
dispatch note shall constitute a lot. Table 2. 


Table 2 Number of Bales to be Selected from a Lot 
(Clause 7.3) 


SINo. No. of Bales in the Lot Sample Size of Bales Number of Bundles

7.3.1 The number of bundles to be selected shall be 
in accordance with col (4) of Table 2. 


7.3.2 One skein shall be drawn from each bundle 
selected. 


7.4 Number of Tests 


7.4.1 For determining linear density one hank shall 
be prepared from each skein selected as in 7.3.2. 
Each hank shall be 25 m in length. 


7.4.2 Breaking load test shall be determined on at 
least 40 test specimens prepared from the skeins 
selected as in 7.3.2 at random. As far as a possible 
equal number of test specimens shall be prepared 
from each skein selected. 


7.4.3 For determining the twist at least 20 test 
specimens shall be prepared. An equal number of 
test specimens shall be prepared from each skein 
selected. 


7.5 Criteria for Conformity 


The lot shall be considered conforming to the 
requirements of this standard if the following 
conditions are satisfied: 


a) From the test results for linear density, the 
average X and range R is determined, and 
the values of the expression X + 0.4 R shall 
lie within the specified requirements; 


b) From the test results for breaking load, the 
average X and the range R is determined, 
and the value of the expression X — 0.4 R is 
greater than or equal to the relevant 
specified requirement; and 


IS 1912 : 2023 


c) From the test result for twist, the average 
X and range R is determined and the value 
of the expression X + 0.4 R is less than or 
equal to the specified requirements. 


X is average of all the observations and R is 
obtained by taking the average of the ranges of 5 
consecutive observations. 


8 PACKING 


8.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the buyer 
and the feller, the twines shall be made into 1.73 m 
(72 inch) or 2.29 m (90 inch) girth skeins each 
weighing approximately 500 g. Suitable number of 
such skeins shall be packed into a bundle weighing 
25 kg. Maximum up to 10 such bundles shall be 
packed in a bale. 


9 MARKING 
9.1 Each bale shall be marked with the following: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Variety of the twine; 

c) Number of plied; 

d) Net mass of the bundle; 

e) Manufacturer's name, initials or trade-mark; 

f) Month and Year of manufacture; and 

g) Any other information required by the law 
in force and/or by the buyers. 


9.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements 
of this standard may be certified as per the 
conformity assessment schemes under the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 
Act, 2016 and the Rules and Regulations framed 
thereunder, and the products may be marked 
with the Standard Mark. 


IS 1912 : 2023

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
